description:
Allow `v::size(n)-signed` / `v::k-signed` segments when appending to the bitstring accumulator. A value outside the signed range of its width raises (a limit; Elixir truncates), matching the decided rule for unsigned segments. Gorilla's anchor writes `<<1::1, 0::1, dod::7-signed>>`; without it the author must write `band(dod, 0x7F)::7`.

Each accepted convenience construct needs: an Elixir-mode meaning, agreement tests (Defk.Case, both modes), and a docs/language.md entry. Decided in 'Which convenience constructs do the six target workloads need?' (defk-dtw.18); sketches on branch prototype/defk-dtw.18-sketches (prototypes/convenience_sketches.exs).

Done when signed segments of widths 1..64 agree with Elixir mode, including the boundary values and the raise just outside them.

comments.text: Decisions: parse/1 segments are now {value, size, signed?}; signed+unsigned in one segment is a bitstring-segment error; error code kept, narrowed to little-endian/float/binary/other. Signed 0-width holds no bits, only 0 fits (as unsigned). Signed range -2^(n-1)..2^(n-1)-1; message 'bitstring segment value v does not fit in n signed bits' (reason :segment_fit). Native: defk_bits_put_signed range-checks with bounds built from 1<<(n-1) (n<=63) and no signed shifts, then masks low n bits (n<64) into the shared unsigned defk_bits_append. Kernel bodies need an acc head (<<acc::bitstring, ...>>) as for unsigned.

title: Signed integer segments in the bitstring accumulator
